title: A cloud run's PR carries its base epic's commits to main as a side effect
description:
PR 49 (epic ko8, Phase 1) was recorded MERGED at 12:02:38 — the same second PR 50 merged — and its merge commit is a commit that was already on the epic branch. Nobody merged 49. The cloud run for epic gj9 was submitted from epic/ko8, so its base_sha was that branch HEAD, tick-run/gj9 descended from it, and merging the run PR to main carried every commit on epic/ko8 along with it. GitHub then marked 49 merged because its commits were all in main.

The outcome happened to be fine here — 49 was green and intended to land — but the mechanism is not: a run opened for one epic can merge an unrelated epic branch to main without that branch being reviewed or its PR approved, and the operator gets no signal that it happened. It also silently violates the config.md rule that epic integration goes through a PR and CI gate, because the gate that ran belonged to a different PR.

Options to weigh: submit runs from the default branch unless an explicit base is given; refuse to open a PR whose diff contains commits outside the run branch; or have the closeout PR body enumerate any commits it carries that the run did not create, so the extra cargo is at least visible. The third is the cheapest and probably wanted regardless of which other option is taken.
